540: // Observable describes a metric about a container that can be observed. For example, memory usage.
541: //
542: // These correspond to Grafana graphs.
543: type Observable struct {
544: 	// Name is a short and human-readable lower_snake_case name describing what is being observed.
545: 	//
546: 	// It must be unique relative to the service name.
547: 	//
548: 	// Good examples:
549: 	//
550: 	//  github_rate_limit_remaining
551: 	// 	search_error_rate
552: 	//
553: 	// Bad examples:
554: 	//
555: 	//  repo_updater_github_rate_limit
556: 	// 	search_error_rate_over_5m
557: 	//
558: 	Name string
559: 
560: 	// Description is a human-readable description of exactly what is being observed.
561: 	// If a query groups by a label (such as with a `sum by(...)`), ensure that this is
562: 	// reflected in the description by noting that this observable is grouped "by ...".
563: 	//
564: 	// Good examples:
565: 	//
566: 	// 	"remaining GitHub API rate limit quota"
567: 	// 	"number of search errors every 5m"
568: 	//  "90th percentile search request duration over 5m"
569: 	//  "internal API error responses every 5m by route"
570: 	//
571: 	// Bad examples:
572: 	//
573: 	// 	"GitHub rate limit"
574: 	// 	"search errors[5m]"
575: 	// 	"P90 search latency"
576: 	//
577: 	Description string
578: 
579: 	// Owner indicates the team that owns this Observable (including its alerts and maintainence).
580: 	Owner ObservableOwner
581: 
582: 	// Query is the actual Prometheus query that should be observed.
583: 	Query string
584: 
585: 	// DataMustExist indicates if the query must return data.
586: 	//
587: 	// For example, repo_updater_memory_usage should always have data present and an alert should
588: 	// fire if for some reason that query is not returning any data, so this would be set to true.
589: 	// In contrast, search_error_rate would depend on users actually performing searches and we
590: 	// would not want an alert to fire if no data was present, so this will not need to be set.
591: 	DataMustExist bool
592: 
593: 	// Warning and Critical alert definitions.
594: 	// Consider adding at least a Warning or Critical alert to each Observable to make it
595: 	// easy to identify when the target of this metric is misbehaving. If no alerts are
596: 	// provided, NoAlert must be set and Interpretation must be provided.
597: 	Warning, Critical *ObservableAlertDefinition
598: 
599: 	// NoAlerts must be set by Observables that do not have any alerts.
600: 	// This ensures the omission of alerts is intentional. If set to true, an Interpretation
601: 	// must be provided in place of PossibleSolutions.
602: 	NoAlert bool
603: 
604: 	// PossibleSolutions is Markdown describing possible solutions in the event that the
605: 	// alert is firing. This field not required if no alerts are attached to this Observable.
606: 	// If there is no clear potential resolution or there is no alert configured, "none"
607: 	// must be explicitly stated.
608: 	//
609: 	// Use the Interpretation field for additional guidance on understanding this Observable
610: 	// that isn't directly related to solving it.
611: 	//
612: 	// Contacting support should not be mentioned as part of a possible solution, as it is
613: 	// communicated elsewhere.
614: 	//
615: 	// To make writing the Markdown more friendly in Go, string literals like this:
616: 	//
617: 	// 	Observable{
618: 	// 		PossibleSolutions: `
619: 	// 			- Foobar 'some code'
620: 	// 		`
621: 	// 	}
622: 	//
623: 	// Becomes:
624: 	//
625: 	// 	- Foobar `some code`
626: 	//
627: 	// In other words:
628: 	//
629: 	// 1. The preceding newline is removed.
630: 	// 2. The indentation in the string literal is removed (based on the last line).
631: 	// 3. Single quotes become backticks.
632: 	// 4. The last line (which is all indention) is removed.
633: 	// 5. Non-list items are converted to a list.
634: 	//
635: 	PossibleSolutions string
636: 
637: 	// Interpretation is Markdown that can serve as a reference for interpreting this
638: 	// observable. For example, Interpretation could provide guidance on what sort of
639: 	// patterns to look for in the observable's graph and document why this observable is
640: 	// useful.
641: 	//
642: 	// If no alerts are configured for an observable, this field is required. If the
643: 	// Description is sufficient to capture what this Observable describes, "none" must be
644: 	// explicitly stated.
645: 	//
646: 	// To make writing the Markdown more friendly in Go, string literal processing as
647: 	// PossibleSolutions is provided, though the output is not converted to a list.
648: 	Interpretation string
649: 
650: 	// Panel provides options for how to render the metric in the Grafana panel.
651: 	// A recommended set of options and customizations are available from the `Panel()`
652: 	// constructor.
653: 	//
654: 	// Additional customizations can be made via `ObservablePanel.With()` for cases where
655: 	// the provided `ObservablePanel` is insufficient - see `ObservablePanelOption` for
656: 	// more details.
657: 	Panel ObservablePanel
658: }
659: 
660: func (o Observable) validate() error {
661: 	if strings.Contains(o.Name, " ") || strings.ToLower(o.Name) != o.Name {
662: 		return errors.Errorf("Name must be in lower_snake_case; found \"%s\"", o.Name)
663: 	}
664: 	if len(o.Description) == 0 {
665: 		return errors.New("Description must be set")
666: 	}
667: 	if first, second := string([]rune(o.Description)[0]), string([]rune(o.Description)[1]); first != strings.ToLower(first) && second == strings.ToLower(second) {
668: 		return errors.Errorf("Description must be lowercase except for acronyms; found \"%s\"", o.Description)
669: 	}
670: 	if o.Owner.name == "" && !o.NoAlert {
671: 		return errors.New("Owner must be defined for observables with alerts")
672: 	}
673: 	if !o.Panel.panelType.validate() {
674: 		return errors.New(`Panel.panelType must be "graph" or "heatmap"`)
675: 	}
676: 
677: 	allAlertsEmpty := o.alertsCount() == 0
678: 	if allAlertsEmpty || o.NoAlert {
679: 		// Ensure lack of alerts is intentional
680: 		if allAlertsEmpty && !o.NoAlert {
681: 			return errors.Errorf("Warning or Critical must be set or explicitly disable alerts with NoAlert")
682: 		} else if !allAlertsEmpty && o.NoAlert {
683: 			return errors.Errorf("An alert is set, but NoAlert is also true")
684: 		}
685: 		// PossibleSolutions if there are no alerts is redundant and likely an error
686: 		if o.PossibleSolutions != "" {
687: 			return errors.Errorf(`PossibleSolutions is not required if no alerts are configured - did you mean to provide an Interpretation instead?`)
688: 		}
689: 		// Interpretation must be provided and valid
690: 		if o.Interpretation == "" {
691: 			return errors.Errorf("Interpretation must be provided if no alerts are set")
692: 		} else if o.Interpretation != "none" {
693: 			if _, err := toMarkdown(o.Interpretation, false); err != nil {
694: 				return errors.Errorf("Interpretation cannot be converted to Markdown: %w", err)
695: 			}
696: 		}
697: 	} else {
698: 		// Ensure alerts are valid
699: 		for alertLevel, alert := range map[string]*ObservableAlertDefinition{
700: 			"Warning":  o.Warning,
701: 			"Critical": o.Critical,
702: 		} {
703: 			if err := alert.validate(); err != nil {
704: 				return errors.Errorf("%s Alert: %w", alertLevel, err)
705: 			}
706: 		}
707: 		// PossibleSolutions must be provided and valid
708: 		if o.PossibleSolutions == "" {
709: 			return errors.Errorf(`PossibleSolutions must list solutions or an explicit "none"`)
710: 		} else if o.PossibleSolutions != "none" {
711: 			if solutions, err := toMarkdown(o.PossibleSolutions, true); err != nil {
712: 				return errors.Errorf("PossibleSolutions cannot be converted to Markdown: %w", err)
713: 			} else if l := strings.ToLower(solutions); strings.Contains(l, "contact support") || strings.Contains(l, "contact us") {
714: 				return errors.Errorf("PossibleSolutions should not include mentions of contacting support")
715: 			}
716: 		}
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	return nil
720: }

matches.text: return errors.Errorf("Name must be in lower_snake_case; found \"%s\"", o.Name)
